turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
You asked for this meeting, Hale, so I'll let you start, but I have a call at 4:40. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. On what basis?
Can I ask something off the record?
There is no off the record, Hale. I'm writing down everything said in this room. Ask, or answer my question.
When was the last time you actually sat with him while he did homework?
You're not asking about the essay, you're asking about my parenting. I'm writing that down too. I asked you on what basis you entered a zero, and I'm still waiting.
Because in my experience, kids who cheat have parents who are too busy to notice.

My son did not cheat, and you've just told me you decided that before you called me. "Kids who cheat have parents who are too busy to notice." That sentence is going to the principal word for word, Hale, so either show me a document or I'm going upstairs now.
